# Dino Ilievski

> Host of Princeps, a show where Dino asks founders and the people building technology one question: how is this meaningful to humans? Previously: congressional fellow, corporate lawyer, med-tech founder.

Contact and guest inquiries: dino.ilievski@gmail.com
X: https://x.com/realkdi
LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/in/realkdi

## Princeps

Princeps is a show of long conversations with founders and tech people about what their work means for the people who will live with it. A new long episode every Tuesday, with shorts and essays through the week. The first episode, "No Grain Doles," airs December 1, 2026. Episodes on YouTube and podcast apps, shorts on YouTube and TikTok, essays on X.

Dino's manifesto, "No Grain Doles" (publishing November 30, 2026): humans need meaningful struggle, alone and together. Good technology pushes people into harder, better struggles; bad technology drains their agency. People want to progress, not a dole.

Prospective guests: email dino.ilievski@gmail.com. The conversation runs 60 to 90 minutes, filmed, in person or remote, with three or four questions shared ahead of time.

## Projects

- [Age of Agents](https://kdi208.github.io/Age-of-Agents/) ([source](https://github.com/kdi208/Age-of-Agents)): An Age of Empires–style control panel for a fleet of AI agents. Each agent is a unit on a map of your codebase.
- [Routine Lab](https://kdi208.github.io/Routine-lab/) ([source](https://github.com/kdi208/Routine-lab)): Edit a training routine, log body measurements, and see what each change is predicted to do to each tape site.
- [STILL](https://umbra-jolly-acre-drift.grok.me): Who you can still become. You are a certain age, in a certain spot. So were they.

## Writing

Full text is hosted on this site.

- [The Robotics Issue Nobody Is Talking About](https://www.dinoilievski.com/writing/the-robotics-issue-nobody-is-talking-about.html) (Oct 18, 2026): Almost nothing is deployed yet, so the humanoid supply chain can still be fixed before it locks in. The safety envelope of a humanoid lives in its firmware and actuators, not in final assembly — and trust has to be answered continuously after deployment: what is actually running on the machine, and would you notice if its behavior changed?
- [The Next Software Industry Is Humans Writing Rules for Agents](https://www.dinoilievski.com/writing/the-next-software-industry-is-humans-writing-rules-for-agents.html) (Oct 14, 2026): Agents that write their own skills do worse than agents with none; human-written skills jump performance 16.6 points. As agents become the layer over the software stack, every layer is an incomplete contract — and unlike other layers, agents have no law, norms, or culture to fill the gaps. The new software industry is humans writing rules, harnesses, and duties for their agents.
- [Your Agent's Duties Shouldn't Belong to Its Vendor](https://www.dinoilievski.com/writing/your-agents-duties-shouldnt-belong-to-its-vendor.html) (Oct 10, 2026): The law treats an AI agent as a tool, so liability lands on whoever deployed it — yet its duties are whatever its vendor configured. Agency law solved the principal-agent problem for humans with limits of authority, records, escalation, and liability. Those duties should be written once by the principal, enforced from outside the agent, and carried everywhere it acts.
